# FlatifyCSS

> A modern flat design CSS framework for the web, inspired by the Duolingo design system. Plain CSS with a small optional JavaScript file, customizable with CSS variables and Sass, with right to left support and accessibility in mind. MIT licensed, made by Amir M. Mohamadi.

Install with `npm install flatifycss` or load it from a CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/flatifycss@2/dist/css/flatify-min.css`. The JavaScript (`flatify-min.js`) is only needed for accordions, alerts, dropdowns, modals, tabs, the show password button and text truncation, and dropdowns need Popper (`@popperjs/core@2`). The same stylesheet works for left to right and right to left pages, set `dir="rtl"` on `<html>`.

- [Introduction](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/intro): FlatifyCSS is the web modern and minimalist flat design library inspired by the Duolingo design system. It respects accessibility and comes with...

## Overview

- [Design system](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/design-system): FlatifyCSS is not a design system itself and it follows the Duolingo design system principles. It is a collection of design system components that...
- [Colors](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/colors): FlatifyCSS comes with a set of predefined colors and color setter helper classes. This page lists all the colors that are related to FlatifyCSS.
- [Typography](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/typography): FlatifyCSS uses Nunito typeface by Vernon Adams for its default typography. For code the default is Fira Code.
- [Responsive](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/responsive): FlatifyCSS comes with some helper mixins to make your website responsive, if you use Sass in this case these mixins simplify the process of...
- [Grid system](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/grid-system): FlatifyCSS does not provide a grid system, in my humble opinion, it is not necessary. At this point in time you can create impressive layouts with...
- [JavaScript](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/javascript): Most of FlatifyCSS is plain CSS, the JavaScript file is only needed for components that open, close or switch: accordions, alerts, dropdowns,...
- [Accessibility](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/a11y): FlatifyCSS respects accessibility. For documentation, attributes like aria- are included with examples and there is always a note for accessibility.
- [Right to left](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/rtl): FlatifyCSS supports the right to left layout, it is done by using inline features of CSS therefore elements are automatically positioned based on...
- [Dark mode](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/darkmode): If you use Sass to develop, there is a predefined placeholder selector for dark mode, this file is in /scss/helpers/_dark-mode.scss, in this file...
- [Customization](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/customization): If you read about development tools you will find out that you can use Sass, so it is possible to customize the basic styles of FlatifyCSS.
- [Development](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/overview/development): FlatifyCSS is written in Sass, which is compiled to CSS & JavaScript using Gulp. This page covers the development process.

- [Radio](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/forms/radio): Radios are used when there are multiple options but the limit is one, users can choose to have one of them.
- [Toggle switch](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/forms/toggle): The toggle switch can be either checkbox or radio, it depends on the use-case and what you want to do.

- [Popovers](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/popover): In fact popovers are dropdown component, make sure first you read and learn about dropdowns.
- [Progress](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/progress): Show the state of something with the progress component of FlatifyCSS, it has its custom HTML, this is not a <progress> because customizing it is...
- [Search bar](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/search-bar): Search bars are mixtures of input with search type and a search button, they are so practical you can change their size of colors based on your needs.

- [Buttons: Buttons](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/buttons/button): Buttons play a big role in any user interface as they give users the ability to interact with the website, so use them carefully.
- [Buttons: Two-layer button](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/buttons/two-layer-button): This is a kind of button that uses the overlay layer concept and shows secondary text on hover/focus.

- [Buttons: Close button](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/buttons/close-button): By adding .close-button to <button> it will be a button with close icon.
- [Buttons: Search button](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/components/buttons/search-button): By adding .search-button to <button> it will be a button with search icon, it is useful when you want to create a search bar.

- [Pulse](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/pulse): .pulse is a helper class that gives animation to the element ::after so it will get users' attention where is it necessary.
- [Overlay layer](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/overlay-layer): It happens that you might want to have a layer that comes over the element content, it can be done with CSS ::before pseudo-element, however, it...
- [Alignment & positioning](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/alignment): Alignment in CSS is a dilemma for beginners, there are tons of ways to achieve it
- [Float](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/float): Floats are old but still the easiest way to let text wrap around an image. FlatifyCSS has three tiny helper classes for them:
- [Containers](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/containers): To have a clean layout using containers to limit the width will be a practical example, there are some predefined container classes that you can use:

- [Opacity setters](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/opacity-setters): Opacity setter classes are practical for any element,
- [Size setters](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/size-setters): FlatifyCSS is designed based on rem for root and em for each element,
- [Width & height setters](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/width-and-height-setters): These setter classes help you set width and height for elements, they are defined in _config.scss file, so you can add more setter classes with...
- [Roundness setters](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/roundness-setters): There are classes to make element edges sharp, round, circle...
- [Text alignment](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/typography): A few helper classes to align text, they work on any element with text inside:
- [Text truncation](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/text-truncation): With text truncation helper class you can limit multiple line to one with three dots, it is even possible to create a toggle to truncate and...
- [Scrollable](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/helpers/scrollable): There are classes to control element overflow, sometimes you want to limit y axis scroll for an element so these classes come in handy.

## Mockups

- [Mockups](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/mockups/intro): Mockups are predefined components without specific functionality. They come in handy when using JavaScript frameworks or libraries like React,...
- [Items group](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/mockups/items-group): With items group mockup you can show a list of items that can be selected by adding the .active class, items can have title, subtitle, and icon.
- [Toast](https://flatifycss.amimomo.me/docs/mockups/toast): To notify users and communicate, you need something look-alike toasts that come on top of each other and will get hidden after an amount of time.
